tools.name: list_vpn_servers
tools.description:
List VPN servers for a site.

Returns {data, totalCount}: every page is drained; data holds the VPN server records verbatim
and totalCount is the upstream total (null when none was reported). The first page's other
envelope fields are kept beside them, and incomplete / incompleteReason are added when a capped
drain stopped short.

VPN servers are offset-paginated (native default page size 25); by default every
page is drained and the complete list is returned as {data, totalCount}. Pass
offset alone for a single manual page. A capped drain is flagged incomplete.

The limit requests a total, gathered automatically in batches up to 200;
_pageSize reports requested count, actual sent sizes per request,
observed effective size and returned count, without capping the total.

Required arguments: host, site.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

offset.description:
Optional zero-based starting record; alone, fetch one page manually.
Example: `25`.

limit.description:
Without offset, the record count gathered from the start in pages of at
most 200; fewer only when the collection ends. With offset, limit is sent
unchanged as one page. The console clamps that page to 200, so fewer can
return while more exist (compare _pageSize requested and returned). Omit
offset and limit to drain all.
Example: `25`.

filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as the
upstream `filter` query parameter for server-side filtering (e.g.
`name.like('*guest*')`). Omitted entirely when unset; applies when draining and
when paging manually.
Example: `metadata.origin.eq('USER_DEFINED')`.

    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "tunnel": {
        "name": "Branch office",
        "vpn_type": "openvpn-vpn",
        "enabled": false,
        "openvpn_remote_host": "203.0.113.10"
      }
    }

structuredContent.description:
Delete a VPN client connection by id. Permanently removes its configuration.

Consequence: the tunnel and its configuration are removed, and traffic routed over it is affected; there is no undo.

Classic REST DELETE network/api/s/{site}/rest/networkconf/{_id}. The id is resolved among the site's vpn-client records first, so an id of another kind is never deleted. Under dry-run policy nothing is deleted; returns {status: "dry_run", deleted: false, message, response (the dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params (query parameters), body}})}.

Example call (delete_vpn_client):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "vpn_client_id": "000000000000000000000102"}

Returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is true, message summarizes the delete, response is the upstream body verbatim.
